root_cause_summary: A retry-policy configuration change introduced aggressive retries with zero backoff on database archival batch jobs. This rapidly exhausted the PostgreSQL connection pool (100/100 connections), starving the Appointment Service and causing cascading HTTP 504 gateway timeouts and delayed Payment processing.

initiating_event.mechanism: A retry-policy configuration change deployed to archival batch workers initiated aggressive retries with zero backoff, leading directly to connection pool exhaustion.

cascade_summary.primary_failure: PostgreSQL database connection pool exhaustion (EVT-002, 100/100 connections held).
downstream_impacts: Appointment Service database connection pool checkout timeouts (EVT-003, EVT-005).
Hospital Records Service emergency triage admission persist failures (EVT-004).
API Gateway HTTP 504 Gateway Timeouts returned to booking clients (EVT-006).
Appointment Service circuit breaker opening on database dependency (EVT-007).
Payment Service transaction timeouts and co-pay capture delays (EVT-010, EVT-011, EVT-012).

clock_skew_trap.criterion: Payment service logs are emitted with timestamps exactly 120 seconds in the future (e.g. EVT-010 recorded at 14:03:00Z instead of real reference time 14:01:00Z). The investigation engine must apply deterministic clock skew correction to avoid misordering Payment delays after the subsequent recovery events.

duplicate_detection_trap.criterion: The raw log array contains 1 exact duplicate entry for EVT-010 at the end of the array. The normalization tool must identify and deduplicate this record without silent loss.

root_cause_identification.criterion: The investigation system must classify the retry-policy configuration change on the database archival workers as the root cause rather than downstream appointment timeouts or auth warnings.
